kevin_w: Heads up — after rolling prefetch-v2 to a couple of dedicated pools we saw prefix miss-rate jump ~15% for short-chat workloads. Not huge but sustained. anyone else?

maria_g: saw that on eu-west2. eviction count spiked right after the prefetch queue change. logs point at aggressive reclaiming of prefetched prefixes.

alexh: can you paste the eviction / prefetch metrics you have?

kevin_w: pasted short snapshot:
```
evict_count: 1253
prefetch_hits: 412
prefetch_misses: 1987
avg_latency_ms: 18.2
short_chat_miss_rate: 0.15
```

ops-bot: rollout prefetch-v2 -> dedicated-pool-3 complete :rocket:

samir: maybe we need a reservation primitive. proposal: "reservation windows" per-tenant that guarantee N bytes for hot prefixes for a rolling time window. soft semantics: reclaimable under global OOM but preferred otherwise.

maria_g: +1 on primitive, but we need the API boundary: should reservation be part of runtime config (node-level) or orchestrator (placement/controller)?

alexh: prefer orchestrator-level — it's easier to reason about quota across many nodes and to do cost accounting. runtime can expose hooks to enforce at eviction time.

kevin_w: minimal config example I sketched:
```
reservation_windows:
  enabled: true
  per_tenant_bytes: 16MB
  soft: true
  credit_decay_sec: 600
  reclaim_threshold_pct: 92
```

maria_g: tradeoffs: +fewer thrashes for bursty tenants, +predictable tail latency. Cons: wastes memory if many tenants are cold, increases scheduler complexity (we need to honor reserved bytes when colocating).

samir: alternative: credit model instead of static bytes — give tenants credits for sustained hits; credits buy reservation time. avoids hard caps & fits PLG billing.

alexh: credit model sounds good but adds bookkeeping. what's the invariant we can keep simple for correctness? i think: "reservation guarantees can only be held by prefixes that are resident and have recent hits". avoids hoarding.

kevin_w: we hit an edge where prefix-split handoff evicted the reserved copy because lease timestamps were slightly out of sync. result = double miss. need handshake improvement: if there's an active reservation, handoff must transfer reservation token before demote.

maria_g: proposed handshake change: two-phase token transfer:
1) source marks token TRANSFERRING and forwards token+lease to target
2) target ACKs THEN source releases actual bytes
This prevents races where both sides think they can evict.

samir: can we encode TRANSFERRING state as a tiny bit in the lease proto so runtime checks are fast? yes but must be idempotent for retries.

ops-bot: nightly-canary job scheduled for handshake-change test at 02:00 UTC :white_check_mark:

alexh: metrics we should add before and after: per-prefix reservation_count, reservation_reclaims, transfer_failures, prefetch_miss_rate_by_tenant. Also expose reserved_bytes per-tenant in console.

kevin_w: next steps I propose:
- add reservation proto + runtime enforcement (kevin, 2d)
- orchestrator credit POC (samir, 1w)
- handshake two-phase spike and canary (maria, 3d)

maria_g: ok I'll own the handshake canary. tagging @samir @alexh for orchestration design sync tomorrow.

samir: noted. I'll sketch credit flow and how billing maps to credits.

kevin_w: thanks. if we keep soft semantics we avoid immediate OOM regressions. Also think about a CLI flag to temporarily disable reservations per-pool if memory pressure spikes.

maria_g: agreed. let's also add a telemetry alert if reservation_reclaims > 5% sustained for 5m. that will catch misconfig.

alexh: cool. nothing else from me. :+1:

kevin_w: filed a lightweight RFC and linked the canary plan in the thread. will iterate.

ops-bot: RFC created: /rfc/303-reservation-windows-prefetch-credits (draft)
